QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_56

question.text: A trader holds a long Nifty futures position worth Rs 10 lakh and a qualifying offsetting position in the cash market (or another derivatives leg) of equivalent Rs 10 lakh that the exchange recognises for cross-margining. Assume initial margin is 15% on each leg and, hypothetically, cross-margining provides a 70% reduction on the offsetting portion. What is the approximate total margin required after the cross-margin benefit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Without any cross-margin benefit, total margin = 15% x Rs 10,00,000 + 15% x Rs 10,00,000 = Rs 3,00,000. Applying the assumed 70% reduction on the offsetting portion: Rs 3,00,000 x (1 - 0.70) = Rs 90,000. The Trap: Rs 3,00,000 ignores the cross-margin benefit; Rs 1,50,000 applies a 50% benefit; Rs 45,000 applies the 70% reduction twice. The workbook supports cross-margining for offsetting positions across cash and derivatives in equity, but it does not prescribe a specific 70% benefit — the 70% used here is purely a hypothetical input to make the arithmetic clean. Note: The exact cross-margin benefit, the eligible position pairs and the haircut treatment are notified by the exchange / clearing corporation; advisors should refer to the live exchange circulars when sizing real positions.
